question: What is a major public health hazard associated with poorly managed healthcare waste?

options.A: Reduction in local potable water salinity

explanation: Discarded sharps present an immediate physical hazard that can lead to puncture wounds and transmission of infectious pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h1)

question: Why does open burning of mixed medical waste create environmental health concerns?

options.A: It releases toxic dioxins into the air
options.B: It immediately floods nearby residential streets
options.C: It causes complete failure of local power grids
options.D: It depletes the soil of essential nitrogen

explanation: Combustion of plastics and chemical residues generates hazardous air pollutants that harm surrounding respiratory health. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h1)

question: At what stage should healthcare waste segregation take place?

options.D: After transport to a recycling plant

explanation: Separating waste immediately where it is produced prevents hazardous materials from contaminating safe domestic refuse. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h2)

question: What happens when hazardous medical waste is mixed with general municipal waste?

options.A: The entire combined volume becomes hazardous waste
options.B: The municipal collectors sort it safely at the dump
options.C: The hazardous elements automatically neutralize over time
options.D: The waste stream safely converts to organic compost

explanation: Contaminating general rubbish with infectious or sharp materials forces the whole load to be treated as high-risk waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h2)

question: What type of container is required for discarding used hypodermic needles?
explanation: Sharps must be placed into rigid, puncture-proof safety boxes to prevent accidental stabs during handling and transport. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h3)

question: What is the primary operational purpose of standardized color-coding in clinical settings?

options.A: To satisfy aesthetic interior design standards in wards
options.B: To enable instant visual recognition of waste categories
options.C: To determine the financial cost of purchasing liners
options.D: To indicate which nurse is on duty in the unit

explanation: Color-coded receptacles allow staff to quickly and accurately discard items into the correct stream without hesitation. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h3)

question: What is a primary clinical benefit of using high-temperature incineration for medical waste?

options.A: Elimination of the need for waste segregation
options.B: Complete recovery of all glass and metal
options.C: Significant reduction in total waste volume
options.D: Conversion of biohazards into livestock feed

explanation: Thermal treatment destroys organic matter and drastically shrinks the physical mass of waste requiring final burial. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h4)

question: Why are secondary combustion chambers heated to higher temperatures than primary chambers?

options.A: To destroy complex organic compounds and noxious gases
options.B: To melt metallic surgical instruments into reusable ingots
options.C: To conserve electrical energy during peak hospital hours
options.D: To dry out wet pathological specimens prior to loading

explanation: Re-burning flue gases at elevated temperatures breaks down hazardous volatile substances before they escape into the atmosphere. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h4)

question: What agent does an autoclave primarily rely on to sterilize infectious waste?
explanation: Autoclaves use heat and pressure to force moisture into microbial cells, effectively destroying them without combustion. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h5)

question: What advantage do non-incineration technologies like autoclaving have over open burning?

options.A: They require zero electrical power or fuel source
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for waste packaging
options.C: They transform infectious waste into drinkable water
options.D: They produce significantly fewer toxic air pollutants

explanation: Steam sterilization and microwave treatment sanitize waste safely without emitting harmful dioxins into the local air. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h5)

question: Which chemical is commonly used for liquid medical waste disinfection in clinical settings?
explanation: Chlorine-based solutions like sodium hypochlorite are widely used to kill infectious agents in liquid waste and surface spills. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of encapsulation in healthcare waste management?

options.A: To compress general refuse into lightweight transport bales
options.B: To immobilize hazardous solids inside a solidifying matrix
options.C: To dissolve sharps into harmless liquid solutions
options.D: To prepare organic specimens for microscopic laboratory review

explanation: Encapsulation locks dangerous materials in cement or similar binders so they cannot leach into the surrounding environment. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h6)

question: What unsafe practice must healthcare workers avoid when handling used hypodermic needles?
explanation: Hand-recapping is a leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries among clinical nursing personnel. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h7)

question: At what point should a sharps safety box be permanently sealed and removed?

options.A: When the outer exterior becomes slightly dusty
options.B: When it reaches three-quarters full capacity
options.C: At the end of every single calendar month
options.D: When every single side is completely jammed

explanation: Stopping at the three-quarter mark prevents overfilling and protects handlers from accidental punctures during sealing. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h7)

question: Which Nigerian agency collaborates in environmental and health waste regulation alongside the Ministry of Environment?
explanation: Regulatory bodies like NAFDAC and environmental protection agencies oversee drug safety and hazardous waste standards. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h8)

question: Why must healthcare facilities provide personal protective equipment to waste handlers?

options.A: To ensure staff remain warm during night shift hours
options.B: To comply with corporate fashion standards in hospitals
options.C: To prevent employees from smoking while on duty
options.D: To shield workers from direct contact with infectious pathogens

explanation: Barrier protection prevents physical exposure to blood, body fluids, and chemical agents during collection and disposal tasks. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h8)
